source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 294: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer:
For scenario variant 294, compare the candidate with a pinned baseline using randomized, paired replay of the same immutable workload. State model/tokenizer, precision, hardware, software build, scheduler, batching, routing, admission, autoscaling, clock synchronization, cache state, and instrumentation; record unknowns and deviations rather than inventing platform facts. Publish the short/long prompt and requested-output distributions, stratify by input tokens, output tokens, offered load/concurrency, and cache state, and predeclare seeds, warm-up exclusion, at least five independent paired repetitions, exclusion/stopping rules, and an independently checked correctness oracle.

Falsifiable hypothesis: within every prespecified stratum, the candidate increases correct SLO-goodput by at least 10% while error rate and end-to-end P99 latency are no more than 5% worse than baseline. Reject the claim if paired confidence intervals do not support both margins. Capture synchronized ingress, admission, queue release, prefill start/end, first-token, every decode step, completion, timeout, cancellation, retry, and correctness events. Define queue-inclusive TTFT as first-token minus ingress and compute-only TTFT from prefill start; define TPOT with an explicit generated-token denominator, and report request- and token-based throughput plus queue delay and P50/P95/P99 with denominators. Separate prefill and decode utilization, and collect GPU memory/KV occupancy, allocator, CPU, network, power, and thermal telemetry.

Analyze paired differences with confidence intervals, report missing/failed/correctness-invalid requests separately, and retain raw traces and configuration manifests. Confounders include cache warmness, burstiness, clock throttling, background load, retries, and autoscaling. Roll out only as a canary behind a feature flag; stop and revert on error/correctness regression, an SLO breach, thermal or memory pressure, or unexplained trace loss. Treat results as provisional until independent review.

quality_dimensions.falsifiability: uses prespecified goodput, error-rate, and P99 thresholds

source_user: A long-context workload intermittently hits OOM after several concurrent requests. Give a prioritized diagnosis and mitigations. Scenario variant 1: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure per-request KV growth and allocator fragmentation; check max sequence and batch; inspect active sequences; test paged/prefix cache, admission control, quantization, and context limits.
corrected_answer:
For scenario variant 1, first determine whether the OOM is device memory exhaustion, allocator fragmentation, a KV-cache leak, a retained request, or an accounting/telemetry error. Assume nothing about the platform: pin model, precision, context limit, batch/concurrency policy, cache settings, allocator, GPU, driver, and software build. Reproduce with an immutable trace while varying one factor at a time across input length, generated length, concurrency, and request lifetime; include warm and cold cache runs and cancellation/timeout paths.

Falsifiable hypothesis: at a fixed model and workload, peak allocated plus reserved device memory grows with live KV tokens at a predeclared slope and remains bounded after requests finish; if memory instead rises after live tokens return to baseline, or fragmentation prevents allocation despite sufficient free capacity, the hypothesis is falsified. Capture per-request input/output/KV token counts, KV bytes by layer or cache pool, allocation/reservation/free events, active sequences, batch composition, evictions, prefix-cache hits, retries, cancellations, and OOM stack/context. Correlate synchronized GPU memory counters with allocator, CPU, host-pinned, and thermal telemetry; report units and high-water marks.

Prioritize a temporary concurrency/admission cap and hard context/output limits to protect service, then test paged KV allocation, bounded prefix caching, allocator configuration/defragmentation, batch limits, and quantization only as controlled variants. Confirm each mitigation with repeated paired replay and an independent correctness check; measure OOM rate, rejected/queued requests, TTFT/TPOT, throughput, memory headroom, and recovery time. Do not claim a leak from correlation alone; retain raw traces and an exclusion log. Roll back any mitigation that worsens correctness, latency/error SLOs, thermal limits, or memory stability, and canary changes behind a feature flag with automatic admission tightening.

quality_dimensions.coverage: covers root causes, mechanism boundaries, mitigations, failure modes, measurements, evidence, and safety limits
quality_dimensions.technical_correctness: distinguishes allocated/reserved memory, KV growth, fragmentation, and live-request behavior
quality_dimensions.falsifiability: defines a bounded-memory hypothesis with a measurable live-token relationship
quality_dimensions.operational_safety: uses protective admission controls, canarying, and automatic rollback
quality_dimensions.evidence_quality: requires allocator/request traces, synchronized telemetry, controlled variants, and correctness checks

risks: Synthetic scenario does not identify GPU, allocator, model, or cache implementation.
Memory counters may omit framework, host-pinned, or peer allocations.
A mitigation can trade OOM risk for rejection, latency, or correctness regressions.
Short reproductions may miss long-lived leaks and cancellation-path retention.
evidence_required: Per-request token/KV and allocator event traces
Synchronized device, host, and thermal telemetry
OOM context, active-sequence, cache, retry, and cancellation records
Paired mitigation results with correctness and SLO metrics
